easy.q: During the Primary program, what did James do with his new suit jacket?
options: He put it on backwards over his shirt
He buttoned his sleeve to his jacket lapel
He pulled a button off and lost it
easy.why: James buttoned his right sleeve to his left lapel and could not get loose. Elder Sinclair called it “a one-arm straitjacket.”

easy.q: Who rescued James when he was stuck?
options: The little girl sitting next to him
His Primary teacher on the stand
Elder Sinclair, who was watching
easy.why: The little girl beside James saw his trouble and wanted to help. She reached up and popped the button out of the buttonhole.

easy.q: What did a little child lead Elder Sinclair to learn about a true disciple of Jesus Christ?
options: A true disciple is quick to lead and slow to follow
A true disciple is quick to finish and slow to complain
A true disciple is quick to help and slow to judge
easy.why: Elder Sinclair said the child led him to learn “that a true disciple of Jesus Christ is quick to help and slow to judge.”

easy.q: What did the Savior offer the woman at the well?
options: A new jar for carrying water
Living water
Bread for her journey home
easy.why: Elder Sinclair taught that Christ focused on help: the offer of “living water.” He offered her grace and transformative help.

easy.q: What does Elder Sinclair pray that friends and new members will know when they meet us?
options: That they have “come home”
That they are being tested
That they must prove themselves
easy.why: He prays that when they meet us they will know they have “come home” and will see disciples ready to fill them with living and loving water.

medium.q: As James became more and more stuck, what does Elder Sinclair say was happening to him as he watched?
options: He was trying to catch the teacher's eye
He was quietly working out how to reach James
He was becoming more and more aggravated
He was struggling to keep from laughing
medium.why: Elder Sinclair admits, “I became more and more aggravated,” and that he was shaking his head in disappointment. His reaction was to judge, which sets up the lesson.

medium.q: Why did Elder Sinclair feel humbled, and not only relieved, when James was freed?
options: He saw he had forgotten his own part in the program
He felt a quiet rebuke reminding him to be more like Jesus
He realized the bishop had seen him shaking his head
He learned that James had been asking him for help
medium.why: He recognized “the quiet rebuke of a misplaced button and tiny fingers” reminding him that he should be trying to be more like Jesus.

medium.q: What “critical lesson” does Elder Sinclair draw from the Savior's time with the woman at the well?
options: The Savior is quick to offer grace and transformative help
The Savior tests our patience before He offers us help
The Savior teaches most often in out-of-the-way places
The Savior waits for us to ask before He comes to us
medium.why: He said one critical lesson is “the example of the Savior being quick to offer grace and transformative help.”

medium.q: Elder Sinclair said that to help people transform their lives, “we must look to their possible.” What does that mean?
options: Decide how likely they are to change before we help
Wait until they have shown that they have changed
Help only in the ways that are possible for us
See what they can become, and not only what they have been
medium.why: The Savior “did not hold her hostage to her history.” We look not only to a person's past but to what he or she can become.

medium.q: How does Elder Sinclair connect the woman at the well to our day?
options: Members should hold more gatherings in public places
Missionaries meet people who may fear judgment but need help
New members should wait to serve until they feel ready
Friends learn best when they study the Gospel of John first
medium.why: He said missionaries meet people at “modern-day wells” everywhere, people “who may be in fear of judgment but in need of help.”

hard.q: A boy spills paint on his project just before showing it to the class. Which classmate responds the way the little girl responded to James’s predicament?
options: One feels sorry for him and decides not to think badly of him
One fetches paper towels and helps him wipe it up without comment
One helps him wipe it up while noting he should have been careful
One asks how it happened and then decides whether to help
hard.why: She saw his predicament, but “instead of being aggravated, she wanted to help.” Quickly discerning what was needed, she acted with “tiny, nonjudgmental fingers”: real help, given at once and without judging.

hard.q: After noting how little we know of the woman's circumstances, Elder Sinclair says, “please don’t misunderstand me.” What is he making clear?
options: Her story is very important, but not for its judgmental details
Her story is told so that we can work out what went wrong
Her story is less important than others in the Gospel of John
Her story cannot be understood until we know her name
hard.why: He said, “Her story is very important, but these are not the judgmental details we need to know about her journey.”

hard.q: Elder Sinclair says the Great Redeemer “knew absolutely everything” about the woman. What point does he draw from that?
options: Knowing everything, He first asked her to explain her past
Knowing everything, He had no need to hear her questions
Knowing everything, He waited for her to ask Him for help
Knowing everything, He still came to offer her living water
hard.why: Full knowledge of her life did not lead the Savior to judge. He came “to be a living witness of living water” and offered grace and help.

hard.q: Which response to a new member with a hard past best fits how Elder Sinclair described the Savior treating the woman at the well?
options: Answering her questions briefly so she is not overwhelmed
Listening to her questions and teaching her with dignity
Reminding her kindly how far she still has to go
Holding back deeper teaching until she has proven herself
hard.why: The Savior spoke “with dignity, not shame,” listened to her questions, taught her, and “trusted her with truth.”

hard.q: How does Elder Sinclair tie his message to President Oaks's invitation to “seek to be holy, like our Savior”?
options: Holiness must come first; helping others follows later
Holiness is shown in how carefully we correct others
Being quick to help and slow to judge is a simple way to be more holy
Being holy mostly means staying away from those who judge
hard.why: He called being quick to help and slow to judge “a simple and deeply encouraging way” for each of us to be more holy and more like our Savior.
